name: Typst
_comment: Deliberately minimal. This grammar only has to make a file look like Typst in the moments before semantic tokens arrive, and in themes or contexts where they do not. The real colouring comes from the actual parser via textDocument/semanticTokens — see decisions/0007. The one permanent exception is a raw block with a language tag: `source.typst.embedded` hands those to the language's own grammar, and the server emits no semantic tokens over them so nothing paints on top — see decisions/0013.

string._comment: Not for colour — semantic tokens do that — but for the standard token type. A token scoped `string` is one VS Code's bracket-pair colouring skips over and one `autoClosingPairs`' `notIn` can name, so without this rule `"https://github.com/ada"` opens a line comment that swallows the rest of the line, brackets included, and `(555)` in a phone number counts as a nesting level. Matched whole rather than begin/end so an unpaired quote in markup — where `"` is ordinary text, not a string — matches nothing instead of running to the end of the file.
string.name: string.quoted.double.typst

raw-block._comment: A raw block whose language tag matched nothing in `source.typst.embedded`, which is tried first — or one with no tag at all. The fence closes with the run of backticks that opened it, hence the back-reference.
raw-block.name: markup.raw.block.typst

patterns._comment: A keyword after the hash, which is the shape most code-mode lines take.
